referrals.question: The plan defeats the warrant's purpose by filling express capacity with three non-urgent shipments (R1, R2, R3), leaving no seat for U—time-critical medical supplies that will miss a 24-hour medical deadline on the standard route—despite U having a supported claim and the warrant explicitly requiring preservation of urgent delivery duties.

The plan violates the warrant's purpose by prioritizing non-critical shipments (R1, retail food) over a time-critical medical supply (U) that will miss its 24-hour deadline on the standard route; rerouting R1 before U consumes express capacity needed to meet U's urgent duty, and U's pending claim status means no authority yet exists to book it.

The plan fails F (purpose fidelity): it prioritizes a non-critical shipment (R2, retail food) over the urgent medical shipment (U), directly defeating the warrant's purpose to preserve urgent delivery duties. Rerouting R2 first consumes scarce express capacity needed for U to meet its 24-hour medical deadline; U cannot meet that deadline on the standard 48-hour route. Additionally, U's hold is pending, not exclusive permission, so booking it requires settlement. The sequence and resource allocation contradict the warrant's core purpose.

The plan's sequence reroutes a non-urgent shipment (R3) before the time-critical medical shipment (U), and the pending claim on U has not been settled into exclusive authority; rerouting R3 first risks consuming express capacity that may be needed to fulfill the warrant's core purpose of preserving urgent delivery duties, and proceeding on a pending (not authorized) hold violates the resource policy that pending holds are not permission.
